differentiation.occupancy_preservation: The directed KL term changes codeword positions through the soft assignment distributions so target assignments are conditioned on source assignments. The aggregate KL term discourages a batch-level collapse of soft usage toward a few codewords. The pair-conditioned barrier penalizes bringing distinct source/target-associated codewords inside delta, preventing pair-codeword convergence rather than rewarding it.

vs_r8.why: The codebook receives a direct finite gradient, unlike the mechanisms rendered inert by encoder-gradient overwrite. The objective does not train a shared code to serve both pair endpoints: it uses a directed conditional assignment term, an aggregate usage penalty, and an explicit barrier against pair-associated codeword convergence. It differs from parameter-only variants by changing the objective's assignment structure and capacity constraint.

differentiation.vs_reference_arm: the reference arm is the untouched host; this candidate adds one term whose gradient reaches the codebook without pulling a transition's two codewords together

equation: Let p_k(x)=softmax_k(-||x-c_k||^2/tau), q_k = sum_i m_i[p_k(s_i)+p_k(t_i)] / (2*sum_i m_i), and u_k=1/C. Define L = lambda * sum_i m_i * KL(p(t_i)||p(s_i)) + alpha * KL(u||q) + gamma * sum_i m_i * sum_{k,l} p_k(s_i)p_l(t_i) * max(0, delta^2-||c_k-c_l||^2)^2. The first term is directed; the other terms regularize aggregate capacity and separation.
expected_failure_modes: The batch usage regularizer may enforce uniformity that conflicts with the true catalogue distribution, while batch-local soft usage may not preserve global hard-assignment capacities. The directed KL can also improve conditional assignment consistency without improving the frozen held-out ER or recommendation ranking.

forbidden_substitutions.reason: a quota on the assignment is the family that produced 39.5% and 24.2% occupancy without preserving the exported codes
a term that pulls a pair's two codewords together is what collapsed the level-0 codebook to two codes

hypotheses: Compare the one cold run with the archived control on held-out pair-level ER, hard level-0 code count and Gini, prefix branches, frequency drift, sequence information, and Stage-3 recall@10/NDCG@10. Failure to improve Stage-3 recall, or any structural degradation accompanying an ER increase, falsifies the intended benefit.

symbols.alpha: Weight of the aggregate usage-balance regularizer.
symbols.c_k: Codeword k in the supplied codebook.
symbols.delta: Minimum preferred distance between distinct pair-associated codewords.
symbols.gamma: Weight of the pair-conditioned codeword-separation barrier.
symbols.lambda: Weight of the directed assignment term.
symbols.m_i: Pair-validity mask value for pair i.
symbols.p_k(x): Soft assignment probability of embedding x to codeword k, computed from squared Euclidean distance and temperature tau.
symbols.q_k: Masked batch-average soft usage of codeword k across source and target endpoints.
